text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- LARGE INTERNATIONAL BANKS COMPETE IN LATIN AMERICA
Large international banks like HSBC are increasingly entering the Latin American banking sector and boosting competition for retail clients and foreign trade financing.
-- CSN COULD ATTRACT PEUGEOT TO RIO

Brazilian steelmaker CSN's plan to supply semi-finished parts to French automaker Peugeot could influence the car manufacturer to build a factory in Resende, Rio de Janeiro state, close to the CSN steelmill.
-- STUDY SAYS BRAZIL'S BLACKS LIVE LIKE IN ZIMBABWE
A study says that the quality of life of blacks in Brazil is comparable to that of citizens of two of Africa's poorest countries, Zimbabwe and Lesotho.
-- MOTTA SEES IRREGULARITIES IN CELLULAR SERVICES
Communications Minister Sergio Motta said the government was looking into irregularities in the trunking system which undermined the cellular phone sector.
-- TELECOMS TO ATTRACT $11 BLN IN INVESTMENTS
Telecommunications companies will invest between $7 billion and $11 billion a year until 1999 on importing equipment to prepare for privatization of the sector.
-- THOUSANDS PAY LAST RESPECTS TO FRIAR DAMIAO

Around 50,000 worshippers paid their last respects to Friar Damiao, considered to be a semi-saint by faithful, filing past his open coffin in the Basilica da Penha in the northeastern Brazilian city of Recife.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
